title: Cross-border phone-fraud corridor — correspondent monitoring (demo script)
summary: Synthetic training case. Over several weeks, a company pays “commission” to dozens of Mainland personal accounts. The payees do not match the supplier list. A correspondent typology indicator links this corridor to phone-fraud proceeds. As a compliance officer, the trainee runs enhanced due diligence (EDD) on the corridor, drafts a suspicious transaction report, or recommends a freeze or an exit. Inspired by public summaries of cross-border phone fraud. It is not a real customer file, and not an actual correspondent file.

teaching.disclaimer: Synthetic training scenario inspired by public enforcement reporting. Not official case files; no real customer data.

sources.label: Police context, April–June 2023 cross-border phone fraud, IRONSPLITTER-related (URL not in the course brief)

rules.when: One customer pays a large number of unrelated Mainland personal accounts, and there is no commission contract
rules.note: Do not release it as ordinary cross-border commission. Rules come before any model score.

rules.when: A correspondent typology indicator links the same corridor to phone-fraud proceeds
rules.note: Do not close the case after the story changes to fees paid on behalf of customers or family living costs. The indicator is a synthetic teaching indicator, not real intelligence.

nodes.title: Commission paid to many personal accounts
nodes.prompt: Over several weeks, Synthetic Consulting Company A pays dozens of Mainland personal accounts. The stated purpose is commission. The payees do not match the supplier list on file.

nodes.title: Look into the corridor?
nodes.prompt: The list already does not match. Do you run enhanced due diligence on the corridor, exit the relationship, or treat this as ordinary cross-border commission?

choices.label: Run EDD on the corridor
choices.rationale: Check the contract and the payee relationships first.

choices.label: Exit the customer relationship
choices.rationale: The supplier list does not match. You can exit without waiting for the next payment.

choices.label: Treat as ordinary cross-border commission
choices.rationale: Teaching override. The missing contract is still a fact. R1 must still be dealt with later.

nodes.title: No commission contract
nodes.prompt: A spot check finds no commission contract. The payees have no business relationship with each other. A synthetic correspondent typology indicator links this corridor to phone-fraud proceeds. Rule R1: this kind of fan-out must not be released as ordinary commission.

nodes.title: Does the fan-out rule allow release?
nodes.prompt: R1 has fired. Do you hold payments and continue the review, draft a suspicious transaction report now, or accept the oral commission story?

choices.label: Hold outbound payments and continue the review
choices.rationale: Matches R1. Stop the fan-out first.

choices.label: Draft a suspicious transaction report
choices.rationale: Payments to many individuals with no contract are already enough to report.

choices.label: Accept the oral commission story and release
choices.rationale: Overrides R1. The typology indicator does not go away because of this.

nodes.title: The typology indicator remains
nodes.prompt: The customer changes the story and says these are fees paid on behalf of customers. The phone-fraud typology indicator has not been withdrawn. Rule R2: when the corridor and the proceeds indicator appear together, do not close the case as ordinary commission or as fees paid for others.

nodes.title: After the indicator appears
nodes.prompt: R2 has fired. Do you recommend a freeze and report, exit the relationship, or accept that these are fees paid on behalf of customers?

choices.label: Recommend a freeze and draft a suspicious transaction report
Accept fees paid on behalf of customers and close
choices.rationale: Poor teaching path. The rule already says the case must not be closed this way.

nodes.title: Suspicious transaction report drafted
nodes.prompt: Reporting exit. The fan-out and the typology indicator stay in the state, so a reviewer can check against them.

nodes.title: Freeze recommended and report drafted
nodes.prompt: Outbound payments are on hold. The report is drafted. If R1 was overridden earlier, the override flag remains.

nodes.title: Customer relationship exited
nodes.prompt: The relationship has ended. The exit does not erase the corridor facts.

nodes.title: Closed as fees paid on behalf of customers
nodes.prompt: Poor teaching path. R2 was ignored. The dashboard should later mark this session as not following the rules.
